subject: social-studies
title: Neighbourhood Change: One Site, Stage by Stage

segments.say: Stage 1: the site as found - houses and open ground. A few low-rise houses stand on open ground and only a few families live here, so the population bar is at its lowest. Point at the population bar on your student notes before the first change lifts it.
questions: What does the site look like at the start, and who lives here?
Why is the population bar at its lowest in this stage?

segments.say: Stage 2: transport arrives first - MRT station and bus stop. The station and bus stop open before any housing blocks rise, so the site is easy to reach, and the population bar climbs one step. Now try the journey question on your worksheet.
questions: What arrives first at the site, before the housing blocks?
Why does it help that transport arrives before homes?

segments.say: Stage 3: blocks rise, then shops, a market and a school open. Housing blocks rise plot by plot on the open ground, families move into the flats, and only then do the shops, market and school open to serve them - the population bar climbs again. Check the stage order against your student notes before moving on.
questions: In what order do the blocks, shops, market and school appear?
Why do the shops, market and school open only after families move in?

segments.say: Stage 4: the wrong turn, corrected - change happens stage by stage. Everything flashes in together, then the true sequence is replayed: transport first, blocks plot by plot, then shops, market and school as families arrive, and the bar climbs to full. Keep the whole order - open ground, transport first, blocks, shops and school - in view as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
questions: What is wrong with the all-at-once version of the change?
What is the whole change, in order, with no stage skipped?
segments.watchFor: A neighbourhood changes all at once, because the new flats, shops and MRT station all appear in a single step. Listen for students who treat the before-and-after photographs as proof that everything appeared overnight. Send them back to the stages: A neighbourhood changes stage by stage: transport links arrive first as the MRT station and bus stop open, housing blocks then rise plot by plot, and only as families move in do the shops, market and school open - the population grows at every stage, not in one jump.
